A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TabReD research work. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison despite the changed title and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original model evaluations on eight TabReD datasets in Table 2, temporal-versus-random split experiments in Figure 1, and an audit of existing datasets.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark evaluations and adds model comparisons, temporal-error and feature-correlation analyses, and statistical ranking results in Tables 3–5 and Figures 1–4.

M1.justification: v3 introduces a causal TabR-S adaptation that restricts training-time retrieval to older observations. v4 removes this adaptation while retaining ordinary TabR. The benchmark construction procedure and temporal adaptations of CORAL and DFR remain unchanged; the newly evaluated literature methods expand the comparisons.

E1.justification: The same eight industrial classification and regression tasks, temporal-versus-random evaluation scenarios, and 100-dataset audit remain. The academic benchmark used for the expanded transfer comparison was already discussed quantitatively in v3. New diagnostics examine existing dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v4 Table 3 adds ModernNCA, MLP aug., MLP aug. rec., MLP ensembles, and MLP-PLR ensembles, substantially expanding comparison across retrieval, training, and ensembling techniques. Causal TabR is removed. CORAL and DFR remain evaluated in the separate Appendix A.3 robustness comparison.

E3.justification: Reported sample and feature counts change across much of the benchmark. For example, Cooking Time changes from 319,986 used samples and 192 features in v3 Appendix D to 228K and 195 in v4 Table 2; Weather changes from 423,795 and 103 to 605K and 98. These are substantive reported setting revisions, without establishing reruns. New diagnostics also introduce temporal error-rate/MAE measurements, ensemble disagreement, and feature-correlation/mutual-information procedures.

E4.justification: New Appendices A.1–A.2 examine how ensemble disagreement relates to errors over time and how feature correlations and target information differ between benchmarks. Section 5.3 expands the earlier performance-margin discussion into a comparison of technique transferability. The causal-retrieval experiment disappears; the random-versus-temporal split experiment and CORAL/DFR analysis are retained.

E5.justification: v4 Appendix C.2 adds a supplementary Tamhane’s T2 multiple-comparison significance test and reports its ranks in Table 5. Both versions already use 15 random initializations and a standard-deviation-based ranking rule. There is no stated increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: v4 adds complete results for five comparison methods, removes causal TabR results, and adds transfer and dataset-diagnostic findings. Most retained models keep identical per-dataset scores, but all eight Trompt scores change: for example, Homesite AUC changes from 0.9546 to 0.9588 and Weather RMSE from 1.5722 to 1.5187. These are reported numerical revisions, not established same-setting gains. Average ranks also change with comparator membership.

T1.justification: Neither version develops theoretical propositions or proofs, and the existing mathematical ranking criterion is retained. The added statistical test and feature analyses introduce empirical procedures without new formal derivations or mathematical guarantees.

C1.justification: The central claims about benchmark gaps, temporal evaluation, and strong GBDT/MLP-embedding performance remain. v4 broadens the transfer claim from architectural advances to training techniques and adds deep ensembles among the successful approaches. Its introduction shifts from progress transferring with smaller margins toward most tested advances failing to transfer.

C2.justification: v4 Section 5.3 adds hypotheses connecting multicollinearity and noisy features to retrieval/augmentation failures, and longer training to memorization under temporal drift. Appendix A.1 explains how falling target noise could improve measured errors despite increasing shift. These substantially extend interpretation beyond v3’s retrieval-specific discussion. Existing industry bias, missing domains, and feature-description limitations are largely relocated.

D1.justification: v3 provides a direct benchmark repository link and states that all datasets are available on Kaggle. v4 removes that link and states that new datasets and detailed datasheets are withheld until acceptance. Exact dataset collection ranges and quantitative tuning-time comparisons also disappear. v4 adds preprocessing-folder instructions and identifies the mutual-information implementation. These are changes in documented access and reproducibility information; actual external availability was not checked.

R1.justification: v4 adds literature on ModernNCA, newer pretraining and MLP methods, ensembles, memorization, and mutual-information estimation, while removing the Saitta–Neri and Wagstaff references. The principal positioning relative to Tabzilla, TableShift, WildTab, and temporal-shift research remains. Consolidated duplicate references do not represent removed research.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Benchmark auditing and construction become separate sections, experiments are reorganized around techniques and transferability, dataset descriptions move into Appendix B, and limitations move earlier. A reproducibility statement replaces the broader-impact ending. The detailed academic-dataset entries remain unchanged apart from formatting.

P2.justification: v4 adds the transfer-comparison chart, temporal diagnostic panels, correlation panels, dataset-summary table, and statistical-rank table. The main performance table is regrouped by technique, and existing CORAL/DFR results receive a separate table. The original split-comparison figure is retained as Figure 2. Typography, headings, citations, and page layout also change throughout.

improvement.justification: The expanded comparisons, shift/feature diagnostics, and additional statistical check strengthen the empirical support for TabReD. However, v4 weakens reproducibility documentation by stating that new datasets are withheld, removing the direct repository pointer and collection ranges, and leaving revised dataset sizes unexplained alongside largely retained scores. These material benefits and harms prevent a reliable net quality judgment from the PDFs alone.
